uops.name: Shift plant quality inspection to AI-first with human escalation
uops.desc: Reconfigure visual inspection across 14 plants from human-primary to AI-primary with human oversight — 620 inspectors shift from per-part review to exception handling and supplier coaching.
uops.back_desc: The highest-visibility workforce decision in the portfolio. Vision models handle conforming parts; inspectors specialize in root-cause and supplier development.

uops.name: Close the AI tooling gap between staff engineers and contract engineering
uops.desc: Meridian's 2,400 staff engineers have full copilot access; 3,100 contract engineers operate restricted. Same drawings, different tools, diverging cycle times — capability amplification, not headcount reduction.
uops.back_desc: Engineering leadership sees 25–40% documented productivity spread between the two populations on comparable change orders.

uops.name: Enterprise AI literacy and adoption program
uops.desc: Adoption of approved AI tools sits at 19% of eligible employees. A structured literacy program with role-specific playbooks raises effective adoption — a prerequisite for most of this portfolio.
uops.back_desc: Every UoP below assumes people actually use the tools. Today four of five don't.

uops.name: Consolidate regional supply planning into one AI-augmented planning desk with senior planners handling exceptions across North America, EMEA, and APAC
uops.desc: Quarterly planning runs in parallel across three regions with 34 planners. An agent ingesting the same inputs surfaces 80% of decisions; senior planners handle regional exceptions.
uops.back_desc: The three regions plan the same SKUs with different spreadsheets. The desk makes exceptions the job, not the spreadsheet.

uops.name: Automate three-way invoice matching in accounts payable
uops.desc: AP processes 70,000 invoices monthly with a 14-person exceptions team. An agent resolving 85% of match exceptions from PO, receipt, and invoice context leaves humans the genuine disputes.
uops.back_desc: Exception queue averages 9 days. The agent clears conforming exceptions same-day.

uops.name: Generate first-draft variance narratives in FP&A
uops.desc: FP&A spends the first four days of each close writing variance narratives. An agent drafting from the ledger and prior commentary cuts narrative time 70%, pointing analysts at drivers instead.
uops.back_desc: Narratives are the close's critical path. Drafting is the part nobody misses.

uops.name: Screening and scheduling agent for high-volume hourly hiring
uops.desc: Talent acquisition screens 160,000 hourly applications yearly across 14 plants. An agent handling screening, scheduling, and reminders cuts time-to-interview from 9 days to 2.
uops.back_desc: Plants lose candidates to faster competitors in the first 72 hours. Speed is the whole game.

uops.name: Agent-assisted dispute resolution in customer care
uops.desc: Care handles 42,000 billing and warranty disputes monthly. An agent proposing resolution packages within policy raises same-day resolution from 55% to a projected 84%.
uops.back_desc: Reps spend most of a dispute hunting context across five systems. The agent brings the context to the rep.

uops.name: Automate freight audit and carrier claims in logistics
uops.desc: Logistics audits 30,000 freight bills monthly by sampling 8%. An agent auditing 100% recovers overbilling the sample misses and files carrier claims automatically.
uops.back_desc: Sampling was a labor constraint, not a strategy. Full audit changes the recovery math.

uops.name: First-draft marketing and product content across brand teams
uops.desc: Marketing produces ~1,900 first-draft assets yearly across four brands. A generative pass with brand guardrails cuts first-draft time 60% and frees the team for campaign strategy.
uops.back_desc: The bottleneck is never the idea. It's the fourth revision of the first draft.

uops.name: Replace tier-1 IT helpdesk with a conversational agent
uops.desc: Helpdesk handles 3,600 tickets weekly, 68% password resets and access requests. A conversational agent resolves those autonomously, freeing the desk for real incident response.
uops.back_desc: Tier-1 volume is dominated by requests with deterministic resolutions. That's agent territory.

uops.name: AI-assisted regulatory submission drafting
uops.desc: Regulatory affairs drafts 340 agency submissions yearly. An agent assembling first drafts from prior submissions and current dossiers cuts drafting effort 50% with reviewer sign-off unchanged.
uops.back_desc: Submissions reuse 70% of their structure. Nobody should be retyping the reusable 70%.

uops.name: Automate warranty claims adjudication
uops.desc: Warranty adjudicates 18,000 claims monthly against policy matrices. An agent adjudicating the 75% of claims that are policy-deterministic leaves adjusters the judgment calls.
uops.back_desc: Deterministic claims don't need adjusters. They need consistent policy application at machine speed.

uops.name: Churn-signal agent for the renewals desk
uops.desc: Renewal reps discover at-risk service contracts too late. An agent watching telemetry, service tickets, and org changes flags risk 90 days out with a suggested play.
uops.back_desc: Every saved contract this year was saved by someone noticing early. The agent makes noticing systematic.

uops.name: Triage supplier inspection reports with a vision-language agent
uops.desc: Supplier quality engineers read 3,400 inspection reports weekly, most conforming. An agent passes conforming reports and routes the 8% with anomalies with findings highlighted.

uops.name: Demand-forecast agent for inventory analysts
uops.desc: Inventory analysts spend ~40% of their week on routine demand reforecasting. An agent handling the routine SKUs focuses analysts on volatile lines and promotions.
uops.back_desc: Routine SKUs reforecast themselves given clean signals. Analysts belong on the volatile 20%.
metrics: 40% of analyst week on routine reforecasts

uops.name: Reskill tier-1 support techs into incident response specialists
uops.desc: With tier-1 automated, 11 displaced techs can be reskilled into incident response, where the backlog is five months. Net-zero workforce impact, higher value per person.
uops.back_desc: The pipeline problem and the backlog problem solve each other.

uops.name: Augment maintenance planners with a parts-and-history agent
uops.desc: Maintenance planners assemble work packets from six systems. An agent pre-assembling parts lists, history, and lockout steps cuts packet time from 50 minutes to 12.
uops.back_desc: Planners are search engines today. The agent gives them back the planning.

uops.name: Apply content-review agents to dealer marketing compliance
uops.desc: Compliance reviews 900 dealer marketing pieces monthly for claims violations. An agent pre-screening against the claims matrix clears the 80% that are clean.

uops.name: Spend-analysis agent for supply chain analysts
uops.desc: Supply chain analysts spend ~60% of each sourcing cycle on spend analysis and supplier benchmarking. An agent ingesting the spend cube produces the analysis pack; analysts negotiate.
uops.back_desc: The analysis pack is table stakes. Negotiation leverage is the job.

uops.name: Add an AI workforce impact review to quarterly board cadence
uops.desc: Directors currently see AI progress as project status. A quarterly workforce-impact review — capacity created, roles redesigned, redeployment outcomes — makes the transition governable.
uops.back_desc: What the board measures, the org manages. Today the board measures pilots.

uops.name: Stand up an AI governance committee with executive ownership
uops.desc: No single owner exists for AI risk appetite, tooling policy, or workforce transition standards. A board-chartered committee with a named executive owner closes the gap.
uops.back_desc: Every UoP in this portfolio eventually routes a decision through a committee that doesn't exist yet.
